items.body: The runner closes its initial output-file handles, then reopens tool-accessible paths with `fs::write(stdout, &output)?`. A tool can replace `check.stdout` with a symlink, causing the runner to truncate/write a file outside scratch. This happens even when `within_budget` detects the symlink: output publication precedes `result?`. Replacing the file with a FIFO can instead block indefinitely.
items.suggestion: Retain securely opened file handles and publish through them. Reject substituted output paths before reopening them, including in Apalache’s error-output reader. Add symlink/FIFO controls.
items.title: The runner closes its initial output-file handles, then reopens tool-accessible paths with `fs::write(stdout, &output)?`

items.body: The new unconditional pipe-reader joins can defeat timeout/cancellation on Darwin. For non-JVM commands, the supervisor only kills the original process group; a descendant that starts another session survives and retains stdout/stderr. The supervisor exits, but `out.join()` waits indefinitely. Selecting the Darwin branch in memory on Linux reproduced both the surviving descendant and missing pipe EOF; all reproducer processes were cleaned up. The previous file-based output collection did not introduce this indefinite join.
items.suggestion: Complete descendant ownership for Darwin helper commands and bound cleanup/drain waits. Add a separate-session descendant control for that path.
